cases.command: mkdir -p /data/ziptime/q && printf y > /data/ziptime/q/b && chmod 750 /data/ziptime/q/b && touch -d '2025-08-13 10:00:00' /data/ziptime/q/b /data/ziptime/q && (cd /data/ziptime && zip -qr /data/ziptime.zip q) && mkdir /data/ziptime/x && (cd /data/ziptime/x && unzip -q /data/ziptime.zip) && stat -c '%a %y %n' /data/ziptime/x/q /data/ziptime/x/q/b
cases.note: zip records each entry's mode and time, and Info-ZIP's unzip restores both, a directory's included.

cases.command: mkdir -p /data/zt/q && printf y > /data/zt/q/b && touch -d '2025-08-13T10:00:00Z' /data/zt/q/b /data/zt/q && cd /data/zt && TZ=Asia/Tokyo zip -qr /data2/zt.zip q && unzip -l /data2/zt.zip | sed -n 4,5p; TZ=Asia/Tokyo unzip -Z /data2/zt.zip | sed -n 3,4p | cut -c 30-; mkdir -p /data/zt/x && cd /data/zt/x && TZ=America/New_York unzip -q /data2/zt.zip && stat -c '%y %n' q q/b
cases.note: zip records each entry's time in UTC beside the DOS time it reads on the session's clock, written across mounts in the session's zone; a listing reads the UTC time in its own zone and unzip lands it in any zone, as Info-ZIP does.
